latest_release.body:
## 💾 Download

Installation:
```bash
npm install pixi.js@8.23.0
```

Development Build:
- https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/pixi.js@8.23.0/dist/pixi.js
- https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/pixi.js@8.23.0/dist/pixi.mjs

Production Build:
- https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/pixi.js@8.23.0/dist/pixi.min.js
- https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/pixi.js@8.23.0/dist/pixi.min.mjs

Documentation:
- https://pixijs.download/v8.23.0/docs/index.html

## Changed
https://github.com/pixijs/pixijs/compare/v8.22.0...v8.23.0

### 🚨 Behavior Change
* fix: deliver global move events to interactive ancestors once and trim per-target dispatch work by @GoodBoyDigital in https://github.com/pixijs/pixijs/pull/12329
  * An interactive ancestor of the object under the pointer, such as an interactive `app.stage`, now receives `globalpointermove`, `globalmousemove` and `globaltouchmove` once per move instead of twice. This applies to listeners and to `on*` handler properties. Code that counted these calls or added up movement per call will see half as many calls.
* chore: merge the PixiJS agent skills into one pixijs skill by @Zyie in https://github.com/pixijs/pixijs/pull/12384
  * PixiJS now ships one `pixijs` agent skill in `node_modules/pixi.js/skills/` in place of the separate `pixijs-*` skills. Point any agent setup that loads or names an old skill, such as `pixijs-scene-sprite`, at `skills/pixijs` instead.

### 🎁 Added
* feat: add SmoothGraphics with shader-based HHAA anti-aliasing by @Zyie in https://github.com/pixijs/pixijs/pull/12002
  * New `SmoothGraphics` is a `Graphics` that anti-aliases its edges in the shader, so shapes and thin lines stay smooth without MSAA, at any scale and inside render textures. It has the same drawing API as `Graphics`, and a `DashLineShader` set as its context's `customShader` draws the strokes dashed and hides the fills, with `dash` and `gap` changeable without rebuilding geometry. A `GraphicsContext` drawn by both a `Graphics` and a `SmoothGraphics` can render blank in one of them without an error, so give one of them a `context.clone()`.
  ```ts
  import { DashLineShader, SmoothGraphics } from 'pixi.js';

  const smooth = new SmoothGraphics()
      .circle(100, 100, 50)
      .fill(0xde3249)
      .stroke({ width: 1, color: 0xffffff });

  const dashed = new SmoothGraphics();

  dashed.context.customShader = new DashLineShader({ dash: 10, gap: 5 });
  dashed.moveTo(0, 0).lineTo(200, 0).stroke({ width: 2, color: 0xffffff });

  app.stage.addChild(smooth, dashed);
  ```
* feat: add safariFontDelay option for HTMLText by @vtxe02023274 in https://github.com/pixijs/pixijs/pull/12324
  * The new `safariFontDelay` renderer option sets how many milliseconds `HTMLText` waits before drawing in Safari, where embedded fonts may not be ready yet. It defaults to 100, the previous fixed delay. Set it to 0 to skip the wait when your fonts are already loaded in the document, at init or later through `renderer.htmlText.safariFontDelay`.
  ```ts
  import { Application } from 'pixi.js';

  const app = new Application();

  // fonts are already loaded in the document, so skip the Safari wait
  await app.init({ safariFontDelay: 0 });

  // or change it later
  app.renderer.htmlText.safariFontDelay = 0;
  ```
* feat: support Chrome 155+ HTML-in-Canvas API by @Zyie in https://github.com/pixijs/pixijs/pull/12341
  * `HTMLSource` now uses the Chrome 155+ HTML-in-Canvas API, `texElementSubImage2D` on WebGL and `drawElementImageToTexture` on WebGPU, and falls back to the older calls, so it keeps working once Chrome removes them. In Chrome 155+ the element can sit anywhere inside the canvas instead of only as a direct child, except on WebGPU in Chrome 156, which still needs a direct child. `HTMLSourceCanvas` now types `updateElementGeometry` and `clearElementGeometry`, which tell the browser where WebGL or WebGPU drew the element so it can hit test it and report it to assistive technology.

# PixiJS ⚡️ > Next-Generation, Fastest HTML5 Creation Engine for the Web - 🚀 [WebGL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WebGL) & [WebGPU](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WebGPU) Renderers - ⚡️ Unmatched Performance & Speed - 🎨 Easy to use, yet powerful API - 📦 Asset Loader - ✋ Full Mouse & Multi-touch Support - ✍️ Flexible Text Rendering - 📐 Versatile Primitive and SVG Drawing - 🖼️ Dynamic Textures - 🎭 Masking - 🪄 Powerful Filters - 🌈 Advanced Blend Modes PixiJS is the fastest, most lightweight 2D library available for the web, working across all devices and allowing you to create rich, interactive graphics and cross-platform applications using WebGL and WebGPU. ### Setup It's easy to get started with PixiJS! Just use our [PixiJS Create](https://pixijs.io/create-pixi/) CLI and get set up in just one command:

``` npm create pixi.js@latest ``` or to add it to an existing project: ``` npm install pixi.js ``` ### Usage ```typescript import { Application, Assets, Sprite } from 'pixi.js'; (async () => { // Create a new application const app = new Application(); // Initialize the application await app.init({ background: '#1099bb', resizeTo: window }); // Append the application canvas to the document body document.body.appendChild(app.canvas); // Load the bunny texture const texture = await Assets.load('https://pixijs.com/assets/bunny.png'); // Create a bunny Sprite const bunny = new Sprite(texture); // Center the sprite's anchor point bunny.anchor.set(0.5); // Move the sprite to the center of the screen bunny.x = app.screen.width / 2; bunny.y = app.screen.height / 2; app.stage.addChild(bunny); // Listen for animate update app.ticker.add((time) => { // Just for fun, let's rotate mr rabbit a little. // * Delta is 1 if running at 100% performance * // * Creates frame-independent transformation * bunny.rotation += 0.1 * time.deltaTime; }); })(); ``` ### TypeScript PixiJS supports WebGPU, so its type declarations depend on the WebGPU types. Where those come from depends on your TypeScript version. **TypeScript 5:** no WebGPU types are built in, so PixiJS adds [`@webgpu/types`](https://github.com/gpuweb/types) for you. No additional setup required. **TypeScript 6 and 7:** the WebGPU types are built into the `"dom"` library, but some releases leave parts out, such as `GPUTextureUsage`. Use [`@types/web`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@types/web), which has the full set, in place of `"dom"`. Remove `@webgpu/types` from `types` if it's there, since it conflicts with the built-in types. ```bash npm install --save-dev @types/web ``` ```json { "compilerOptions": { "lib": ["esnext"], "types": ["@types/web"] } } ``` ### Contribute Want to be part of the PixiJS project? Great! All are welcome! We will get there quicker together :) Whether you find a bug, have a great feature request, or you fancy owning a task from the road map above, feel free to get in touch. Make sure to read the [Contributing Guide](.github/CONTRIBUTING.md) before submitting changes. ### License This content is released under the [MIT License](http://opensource.org/licenses/MIT). ### Change Log [Releases](https://github.com/pixijs/pixijs/releases)
